subject: ACME - feature parity & competitive eval follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME - initial post-call recap + next steps (feature parity / competitive tests)

Thanks for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the evaluation moving quickly.

Call highlights:
- ACME is validating feature parity for tool/function calling, structured outputs (strict JSON schemas), and streaming responses.
- Primary comparison targets: Hyperscaler A's inference API and the incumbent vendor (your internal benchmark). You also want cost/latency numbers for Redwood Dedicated vs hosted.
- Security/compliance checks are still in flight (SOC2, data retention questions).

Proposed tests (we think these will give the most signal):
1) Tool/function calling: run a 3-scenario test where Redwood calls back to ACME mock tools (CRUD + external API call) and verify end-to-end traces + reliability under concurrent sessions.
2) Structured output / schema adherence: 500 prompt samples with expected JSON schema; measure validation pass rate and necessary prompt engineering.
3) Streaming: compare end-to-end time-to-first-token and average tail latency for 1k prompt set across Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated (pinned), and Hyperscaler A.
4) Cost/throughput: sample workload run to estimate token cost and 95th percentile latency.

Attached: acme-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf (high-level comparison) and a test-plan template (acme-test-plan-matrix.xlsx) to capture your sample prompts, expected schemas, and priority scenarios.

Next steps:
- Alicia / Tom: confirm priority of tests and share the sample prompt set or a small representative subset (10–20 prompts) by EOD Wed.
- ACME security: if you want, we can provide the SOC2 snapshot and an example data retention policy — looping Neha for security coordination.
- Redwood: Nikhil and I will finalize the test harness and confirm resource needs (Dedicated vs hosted).

If that sounds right I’ll schedule the first smoke test for next week (Nov 23–24).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf]
[Attachment: acme-test-plan-matrix.xlsx]

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - initial post-call recap + next steps (feature parity / competitive tests)

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed.

Quick answers:
- Priority: structured outputs > tool-calling > streaming for visibility, but we care about all three.
- I can share a representative set of 15 prompts and expected schemas by end of day Wednesday (Nov 18).
- Security: our InfoSec will need the SOC2 snapshot + encryption details; please send to infosec@acme.com (I copied Tom as the technical owner).

We also want to better understand the Dedicated option cost profile vs hosted for predictable throughput — a short slide on that would be great.

Appreciate you looping in Neha/Nikhil. Looking forward to the test plan.

Best,
Alicia
Dir. Product, Acme Corp
[Inline: short note — we’ll prioritize the schema tests]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - initial post-call recap + next steps (feature parity / competitive tests)

Great — thank you, Alicia. Looping in Neha and Nikhil for technical coordination and to propose a concrete test schedule.

Hi Neha / Nikhil — below is a proposed mutual action plan and a breakdown of the tests with what we need from ACME. Please review and flag anything missing.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
- Wed 11/18: ACME shares representative prompts + expected JSON schemas (15 items) — Alicia/Tom
- Thu 11/19: Redwood prepares test harness and confirms resource allocation; sends SOC2 snapshot to ACME infosec — Neha
- Mon 11/23: Smoke tests (small-run) for structured outputs and tool-calling (streaming optional) — Redwood runs hosted + Dedicated smoke comparisons
- Tue 11/24: Full 500-sample structured output run + streaming batch test (if smoke looks good)
- Fri 11/27: Results review and decision on next steps / pilot commit

Test details (what Redwood will measure):
- Schema adherence (pass/fail + error categories)
- Time-to-first-token and 95th percentile tail latency (streaming enabled vs disabled)
- Function call success rate and call-side error classification (timeouts, malformed payloads)
- Token cost estimates for each run (hosted vs Dedicated estimate)

What we need from ACME:
1) Representative prompt set (15 items) with expected schema + a short note on acceptable error types.
2) A small mock tool endpoint (or sample responses) for function-calling scenarios (we can also run using Redwood-hosted mock if you prefer).
3) Confirmation if any of the samples include PII or sensitive data (affects test environment configuration).

Attachments: I updated the test-plan matrix with explicit columns for expected schema, priority, and mock tool URL.

Neha — can you confirm we can get SOC2 snapshot to Alicia’s infosec, and also whether we need a data processing addendum before we run sample tests?

Nikhil — for the streaming test, we’ll need to define: max concurrent sessions (suggest 50), typical prompt length, and expected KV-cache behavior (are prompts often continuing previous context?).

Thanks — I’ll hold a 30-min sync Thurs 11/19 at 11am PT if that works for everyone (invite to follow).

—Marissa
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-test-plan-matrix.xlsx]

From: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME - initial post-call recap + next steps (feature parity / competitive tests)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. I’m attaching the 15 sample prompts and expected schemas as promised (separate email to follow with the files).

A couple quick clarifications:
- For tool-calling tests please run a scenario where the model must call tool A (lookup inventory) and then tool B (create order) in the same session — we want to see how function-calling state is managed across chained calls.
- For streaming: yes, time-to-first-token is critical for our UX. If you can provide both the hosted and Dedicated timing we’ll be able to make a quick comparison.

We don’t expect PII in these samples, so no special handling required for the initial runs.

Looking forward to the smoke test next week.

Tom
Senior Engineer, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme-sample-prompts-15.json]
